name: Langfuse
tagline: MCP-Native Agent Eval vs SDK-Based Tracing
oneLine: Open-source AI engineering platform for debugging, analyzing and iterating on AI agent applications; part of ClickHouse since January 2026.
tldrVendor: Langfuse is an open-source AI engineering platform with native Python/JS SDKs, 100+ library/framework integrations, prompt management, and enterprise compliance (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA). If you need broad framework support, prompt versioning, or enterprise certifications today, Langfuse is the more established choice.

rows.quote: The observe decorator is an easy way to automatically capture inputs, outputs, timings, and errors of a wrapped function without modifying the function's internal logic.
Clickhouse: High-performance OLAP database which stores traces, observations, and scores.

rows.vendor: Async SDK tracing in your process
rows.quote: As the Langfuse SDKs are asynchronous, they buffer observations in the background.

rows.vendor: LLM-as-a-Judge, human annotation, custom scores via API/SDK, and server-side code evaluators (deterministic Python or TypeScript)
rows.quote: If you want Langfuse to run deterministic Python or TypeScript logic for you, use code evaluators

rows.vendor: Usage and USD cost per LLM call; dashboards and Metrics API by model, tags, or user
rows.quote: Langfuse tracks the usage and cost of every LLM call in your application, so you can monitor spend across models, use cases, and over time.

rows.vendor: Hosted MCP server: create scores, evaluators and evaluation rules; query observations and datasets
rows.quote: investigate a production issue, pull the relevant observation details, compare metrics, create or update scores, add comments for the team, or prepare dataset items for regression testing.
This repository is MIT licensed, except for the `ee` folders.
Group by user, model, time, trace name, etc.

rows.vendor: 100+ library/framework integrations, plus native Python/JS SDKs and OpenTelemetry
rows.quote: Capture traces via our native SDKs for Python/JS, 100+ library/framework integrations, OpenTelemetry, or via an LLM Gateway such as LiteLLM

rows.vendor: Versioned prompts with labels for environment deployment; client-side SDK caching
rows.quote: Use version control and labels to manage deployments across environments
covered by SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 audits, and undergoes annual third-party penetration tests

rows.vendor: Cloud: Hobby free (50k units a month, 30 days data access), Core $29/month, Pro $199/month, Enterprise $2,499/month; the MIT core is free to self-host

vendorReasons.text: You need prompt management and versioning
You need LLM-as-Judge evaluation (semantic, not just heuristic)
You need enterprise compliance today (SOC 2, HIPAA)
You're using non-MCP frameworks and need broad SDK support
You need multi-dimension dashboard slicing (user, session, model)

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and Langfuse?
faq.vendorPart: Langfuse is an open-source AI engineering platform with native Python/JS SDKs and @observe decorators, prompt management, and 100+ library/framework integrations. Langfuse offers broader framework support and enterprise compliance (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA).

faq.question: Is Iris better than Langfuse for MCP agent evaluation?
faq.vendorPart: Langfuse requires instrumentation through its SDKs, a framework integration, or OpenTelemetry, and offers LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation, human annotation, and enterprise compliance.
